brief: We have an urgent launch date in the next six months, but our development team is spending, on average, 25% of their time on fixing legacy code. We need to find a way to reduce the amount of time spent on these bug fixes and suboptimal functionality, or increase our development velocity, as at the moment we are looking like we're going to miss our next feature launch deadline by at least a month and possibly two. We currently have six mid-weight developers.

unknowns: The forecast says the launch could be missed by at least one month and possibly two. What delivery date is currently forecast, and what is the exact launch deadline?

Olumi's proposed legacy-code reduction option assumes that reducing time on legacy fixes from 25% to 15% is feasible; what level of legacy-fix time is realistic without increasing customer or operational risk?

Olumi's proposed hiring option assumes two additional mid-weight developers, contributing roughly 8% of the launch deliverable per month after a 2–4 month lead time. What hiring, notice, onboarding and ramp-up timing is realistic?
Which legacy-code work is essential defect remediation versus suboptimal functionality that can be deferred, redesigned or retired?
